value.lineage: BDWGC (1988-, Hans Boehm, Alan Demers, Mark Weiser): a conservative mark-sweep (optionally generational, incremental, parallel) garbage collector usable as a drop-in malloc replacement for C/C++; the GC behind many language runtimes

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: automatic memory reclamation without language support

value.built_to: reclaim unreachable heap memory automatically in a language (C/C++) that gives the collector no cooperation -- scanning the stack and heap conservatively for anything that looks like a pointer
value.pressure: no type information about what is a pointer; must never free reachable memory (soundness) while freeing most garbage (completeness) without stopping the program too long
value.success_means: no use-after-free of live objects, bounded pause times, and most garbage reclaimed; gctest passes

ANCESTRY.value: BDWGC (1988-, Hans Boehm, Alan Demers, Mark Weiser): a conservative mark-sweep (optionally generational, incremental, parallel) garbage collector usable as a drop-in malloc replacement for C/C++; the GC behind many language runtimes

cut.note: a mark-sweep collector that never knows which words are pointers: every word in a reachable object (or the stack) whose value falls inside the heap's plausible address range and resolves through a two-level block index to a live block header is treated as a pointer; the cost of that guess is bounded by black-listing pages that false pointers have hit; collection is triggered by bytes allocated since the last GC exceeding a fraction of the estimated scan work

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: GC_mark_from (518-640): mse_start / mse_descr; GC_DS_LENGTH (split at 128 words), GC_DS_BITMAP (one bit per word says 'may be a pointer'), GC_DS_PROC; credit = HBLKSIZE
organs.mechanism: the mark stack holds (start, descriptor) entries; a descriptor is a length (scan every word), a bitmap (scan flagged words: the 'typed' allocation hook), or a procedure; long ranges are split so the stack does not explode (and, under PARALLEL_MARK, halved for stealing); each candidate word is range-checked against the least/greatest plausible heap address, prefetched, then pushed via the header lookup; the loop runs until the stack is empty or a byte credit is spent, so marking can be resumed (the incremental hook)
organs.output: mark bits set in block headers
organs.state: the mark stack (grown on overflow, GC_signal_mark_stack_overflow)
assumptions: a fast range test rejects most non-pointers before the header lookup; splitting ranges bounds stack depth independently of object size
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: marking cost is per candidate word with a cheap first filter; the same loop serves precise (bitmap) and conservative (length) objects
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: everything that looks like a pointer is retained (the conservative premise); large integer-heavy objects (GC_DS_LENGTH) are scanned in full unless allocated atomic
organs.human_prior: Boehm & Weiser 1988 'Garbage collection in an uncooperative environment'

organs.human_name: headers.c GC_find_header / GC_header_cache_miss / get_index (28-262): GC_top_index[hi] -> bottom_index -> hdr; IS_FORWARDING_ADDR_OR_NIL; GC_all_interior_pointers -> GC_base; mark.c GC_mark_and_push (1343-1360) with HBLK_IS_FREE and the black-list add
organs.mechanism: the address space is indexed in two levels (a top array by high bits, optionally hashed, and per-top-entry bottom arrays of per-block header pointers); a candidate word's block is looked up; a nil or forwarding entry means not a heap object (or, for large objects spanning blocks, the forwarding count walks back to the first block); if interior pointers are allowed, GC_base finds the object start; a free block or no header means the word was not a pointer, and the (page, source) pair is added to a black list; otherwise the object's mark bit is set and it is pushed; a small header cache fronts the index
organs.output: an object to mark, or nothing
organs.state: the index; the header cache; the black lists
assumptions: block headers are allocated out of line so a stray write cannot corrupt them; the index answers 'is this a heap pointer' in O(1) for any word, which is what makes conservatism affordable
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no cooperation from the compiler or the program: any C object can be collected
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: false retention is the known cost, bounded by the black lists and by the allocator avoiding black-listed pages for large objects (the comment: false hits from the stack 'can pin a large object that spans the block')
organs.human_prior: the 1988 paper's 'page table' plus Boehm's later black-listing (1993 'Space efficient conservative garbage collection')
organs.source_boundary: headers.c + the push functions + blacklst.c's interface

organs.human_name: alloc.c min_bytes_allocd (309-350): scan_size = 2 composite + atomic/4 + 2 stack + roots; result = scan_size / GC_free_space_divisor (halved if incremental); GC_should_collect (430-456); GC_expand_hp_inner (1562-1628): expansion_slop, GC_collect_at_heapsize, the plausible-address bounds
organs.mechanism: a collection is due when the adjusted bytes allocated since the last GC reach an estimate of the marking work (composite bytes counted twice, atomic bytes a quarter, stacks twice, roots once) divided by the free-space divisor (default 3), or when the heap reaches a size set at the last expansion; expanding the heap adds a slop (the same estimate plus a constant) to the plausible-address bounds so black-listing keeps working, and schedules the next forced collection just before the slop would be consumed; a maximum heap size can refuse expansion
organs.output: collect now / not yet; grow / refuse
organs.update: per allocation that finds no free object
assumptions: the cost of a GC is proportional to what must be scanned, so amortising it against allocation keeps GC time a bounded fraction of mutator time (the divisor is that fraction's knob)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no explicit GC calls; the heap grows only when collection did not free enough
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a program whose live set grows steadily collects more and more often before each expansion (the 'GC before growing' policy); GC_free_space_divisor trades space for time explicitly
organs.human_prior: the standard allocation-triggered policy; the scan-work weighting is Boehm's

organs.human_name: reclaim.c GC_reclaim_clear (180-212): walk a block by sz, unmarked objects linked onto the free list and cleared; allchblk.c GC_freehblk (934-993): merge with successor and predecessor free blocks
organs.mechanism: small objects live in blocks of a single size class; after marking, a block is swept only when its size class's free list is empty (lazy), by walking the block and threading every unmarked object onto the list (optionally clearing it); a block with no marks is returned whole; large blocks are freed into a free list keyed by size and merged with a free successor (by address) and a free predecessor (found via the header index), with the merged header removed
organs.state: the free lists per size class; the large-block lists
organs.update: per allocation miss / per large free
assumptions: sweeping on demand spreads the cost across allocations; size-segregated blocks make the sweep a stride walk
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: no sweep pause; allocation from a free list is a pop

rejected_cuts.candidate: incremental and generational collection (dirty-page tracking in os_dep.c, GC_collect_a_little), the parallel marker (mark.c 807-1140: work stealing from a shared mark stack), finalisation (finalize.c), thread stop-the-world (pthread_stop_world.c, win32_threads.c), typed and gcj allocation, the malloc/realloc front ends, leak detection, dyn_load
rejected_cuts.note: the parallel marker and the incremental dirty-bit scheme are each a mechanism family; a DEEP pass should take them separately

rejected_cuts.evidence: marking, pointer identification, triggering and sweeping are four files with four separable policies

pressures.condition: an organism manages a heap for a program that gives no type information and may hold pointers anywhere in registers, stacks and objects; it must free unreachable memory, never free reachable memory, and keep its own time and the memory it wrongly retains bounded
pressures.resource_or_constraint: the heap; a per-word test budget
pressures.failure_condition: freeing a reachable object (unsafe), or retention/pause growing with heap size
pressures.world_punishes: treating every word as a pointer with no index (unbounded scan); treating none (leaks everything)
pressures.world_rewards: a range filter plus an O(1) block index; black-listing false hits; allocation-proportional triggering
pressures.observable_consequence: bytes falsely retained and GC time fraction vs heap size, on a program that stores random integers in large arrays (the conservative worst case), with black-listing on and off and with the free-space divisor varied
pressures.vacuity_condition: a program that keeps no integers that look like addresses
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a precise collector with compiler cooperation (which the world must withhold)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given precise pointer maps must retain zero false bytes (the bound); with black-listing disabled false retention on the integer-array program must rise; with the divisor at 1 GC time must dominate: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: memory management for uncooperative languages (Boehm, Demers, Weiser 1988-)

ancestry_edges.to: Boehm & Weiser 1988; black lists Boehm 1993; parallel and incremental extensions later (Boehm, Demers, Shenker 1991 for the incremental scheme)
ancestry_edges.note: from the source headers and the record

unexplained: incremental, generational, parallel and threaded paths unread
